title: Shape of strings that fail to parse
statement: If the aligned pair parser returns no result on a finite Boolean string $z$, then there are finite Boolean strings $w$ and $\tau$ such that $z$ is the concatenation of the doubled string $\mathrm{dbl}(w)$ and $\tau$, and either $\tau$ is empty, consists of one bit, or begins with $10$.
hypotheses_covered: The aligned pair parser returns no result on $z$
replaced:
Consider the aligned pair parser on bit strings, which reads aligned
two-bit blocks from the left, treats the blocks $00$ and $11$ as data bits
$0$ and $1$, and stops successfully at the first aligned block $01$.  If the
parser fails on a bit string $z$, then $z = \mathrm{dbl}(w)\,\tau$ for some
bit string $w$ (with $\mathrm{dbl}(w)$ denoting $w$ with every bit written
twice) and some tail $\tau$ that is either empty, a single bit, or begins
with the bits $1$ then $0$.
